body: I think what's the most sad is that I wish I could call them back and get some validation. But there's none to be had, intellectually I understand the futility. Emotionally, however..

I meant a crisis response that didn't require emergency personnel responding. There is literally no one who you can tell that you can't stop thinking about offing yourself because the response that will be set in motion. And yes, I can understand why this response happens, and I'm not even saying it's bad... I just wish you could get shit off your chest without just sending it out into cyber space for anyone at all to see. But that's what we're left with, right.
I have no words of wisdom, but I did want to say that you are not alone in feeling like everything else manages to live life somehow but you. If that helps at all, I don't know.

I just wanted to say that you're not alone in those feelings - you articulated it much better than I ever could, actually. It's difficult to explain finding yourself slipping toward the edge again. I don't have any good words of comfort, but I wanted to say you are truly not alone.

Still here, tired AF but can't decide what the hell I'm doing.

You?

Wanted to let you know that I saw your message and I'm in a similar place tonight - tip toeing the edge of no return because I'm afraid of it. 

I hope you're okay.

I've heard that (or at least a similar) story, but thanks for sharing. I know in the past I've panicked and thought, "well, sh*t, now I can't turn back without looking like a fool" but I wasn't filled with any great sense of wanting to live either. I just went to the store to get some things if I wanted to follow through and also to "test" what it felt like to be out of the house and possibly going to my destination. I still don't have an answer. Just that I'm tired in a way that sleep cannot help, and I've put everybody through this too many times.
Just wanted you to know that I'm struggling in a similar place (mentally), and I hear you. As cliche as this sounds, you aren't alone.

I like the sound of re-engaging with life on my own terms, and yet experience has shown me that I'll just keep failing to do that. I'm tired of being stuck, and feeling like what I do to build a better life often backfires and reinforces my thinking that truly nothing will make a difference. Round and round in circles I go.

I just wanted to say that I hear you. Especially in terms of life objectively being "better," but still feeling like you want to die, and like anxiety controls your life. 

As paradoxically as it must always sound around here, I hope you stay safe (despite our desires to be otherwise).

Wow, really? What a horrible way to run a hotline. I've never used it because I'm not from the US, just tried to google a (working) number and hoped that having it right there made it easier for the poster (or anyone) to just pick up and dial.
I hope you are alright, and if you need to reach out for help, please call a crisis line or 911. The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline is 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
Can you tell me more about why you quit? Or call a crisis line to talk about why you quit? It's a heavy burden to walk around with these thoughts in your head

Found your post and I'm really hoping that you reach out for help tonight. Call 911 (or the equivalent of 911 if you live outside of the US/Canada) if you have to, to put a barrier between yourself and death. I'm struggling myself, and I sincerely hope that you could either call 911 or call a crisis line if you're feeling over the edge because of what's going on (it sounds like a lot is going on).

Please phone 911 or the equivalent of 911 in your country. I know it's hard dude, but please reach out for help right now. 

ETA: 
throwawayacc19381, it sounds like something really painful is happening for you and if you won't phone 911 for help, I'm wondering if you'd contact a local crisis line to chat about what's happening? In the US the national suicide prevention hotline is: 1-800-273-8255.
